review.summary: Audit of the linearized periodic triangular-network mechanics, conjugate-gradient (CG) quasistatic equilibrium solver, stiffness-matching normalization, and relaxation null controls shows that the quadratic energy assembly and analytic stress derivatives are self-consistent (passing finite-difference gradient and translational invariance checks to ~1e-16, with production force residuals <= 3.31e-10) and elastic controls (r=1) retain 100% of initial stress. However, three structural issues limit the mechanical interpretation of the campaign: (1) because initial modulus G0 (at gamma=0.001) and initial hold stress s0 (at gamma=0.1) are both solved on the identical linear system at q=0, s0 is identically 0.1*G0 and matched_final_stress (s/G0) is algebraically redundant with 0.1*retention (s/s0), while uniform energy rescaling does not interact with the strain-driven memory rate exp(10*abs(e-q)); (2) the analytic homogeneous relaxation nulls (exp(-5) and r+(1-r)*exp(-5)) assume a linear unit rate lambda=1, confounding selective axial-vs-bending stress partitioning with the nonlinear strain-accelerated rate exp(10*abs(e-q)) > 1, while the central-force control (kappa=0) was only run at r=1.0 rather than r=0.5; and (3) 56.5% of production cases are excluded by the eligibility gate, leaving 0 of 4 eligible pairs at L=24, z_target=2.4 across all contrasts and restricting surviving L=24 contrasts to high-coordination regimes ( such as z_target=4.8).

findings.title: Algebraic redundancy of matched_final_stress and retention under linear initial solve and strain-only memory
findings.evidence: In source/cpu-sweep.py lines 95 and 100, G0 is evaluated as s(0.001)/0.001 and s0 as s(0.1) at q=0 on the same linear system H*u = -gamma*B.T@aff, so s0 = 0.1*G0 up to CG tolerance and matched_final_stress (s/G0) equals 0.1*retention (0.1*s/s0), as confirmed across all contrasts in analysis/SUMMARY.json lines 1552-1612.
findings.implication: Uniformly rescaling microscopic energy to match G0 (ACTUAL_DESIGN.md line 13) leaves the dimensionless equilibrium strain e(t) and the strain-driven relaxation law exp(10*abs(e-q)) completely invariant. Consequently, matched_final_stress provides no independent mechanical information beyond retention, and energy rescaling does not test matched macroscopic stiffness under force-activated bond relaxation.
findings.recommended_check: Treat matched_final_stress as an exact rescaling (0.1 * retention) rather than an independent metric; to test stiffness-matched relaxation under force-sensitive kinetics, couple the memory rate to rescaled local force (G_target/G0)*abs(e-q) or match G0 across graph arms by tuning z or kappa at fixed fiber stiffness.

findings.title: Confounded analytic homogeneous relaxation nulls and missing kappa=0, r=0.5 numerical control
findings.evidence: Line 98 updates internal slip q using the nonlinear strain-dependent rate exp(minimum(30, 10*abs(e-q))), which exceeds 1 whenever abs(e-q) > 0, whereas the analytic nulls exp(-5) (line 100) and r+(1-r)*exp(-5) (analysis/SUMMARY.json line 18) assume a constant linear rate lambda=1; meanwhile, source/central.py line 110 runs kappa=0 only at r=1.0.
findings.implication: Deviations of selective relaxation (r=0.5, kappa>0) from the analytic null r+(1-r)*exp(-5) conflate two distinct mechanisms: (a) selective axial relaxation versus unrelaxed bending energy, and (b) accelerated relaxation from exp(10*abs(e-q)) > 1 at gamma=0.1. Because source/central.py omitted r=0.5 at kappa=0, there is no numerical baseline for pure-axial networks undergoing the same nonlinear relaxation law.
findings.recommended_check: Run source/central.py at kappa=0, r=0.5 across all 336 graph variants to establish the true pure-axial numerical relaxation baseline under exp(10*abs(e-q)), and/or run a linear-rate control exp(-dt) to isolate selective bending retention from nonlinear rate acceleration.

findings.title: Complete attrition of L=24, z_target=2.4 matched contrasts and 56.5% overall case exclusion
findings.evidence: Only 584 of 1,344 converged production cases are marked eligible (line 12), and in selected_contrasts (lines 1451-1504) every L=24, z_target=2.4 contrast (both hub_minus_uniform and triangle_high_minus_low at kappa=0.0, 0.003, and 0.03) has eligible_pairs = 0 out of 4.
findings.implication: Although triangle arms 1 and 2 wrap the periodic domain at L=24, z_target=2.4 (wrap_basis_1_mean = 1.0, wrap_basis_2_mean = 1.0 in lines 1208-1226), no matched pairs survive at z_target=2.4. Any conclusions regarding topological control of stress retention are therefore restricted to well-connected, high-coordination regimes (such as z_target=4.8) and cannot support claims near the sub-isostatic rigidity threshold.
findings.recommended_check: Report the exact per-arm G0 values and exclusion reasons for each (L, z_target, kappa, arm) cell, and compute pairwise eligibility for triangle_high_minus_low (arm 1 vs arm 2) without conditioning on whether the fragmented hub arm (arm 3) or the kappa=0 control is rigid.

findings.title: Collinear-only bending formulation and unpinned singular Hessian in CG equilibrium
findings.evidence: Lines 74-80 construct the bending matrix D only for collinear consecutive edges sharing the same direction index d, and line 81 forms H = B.T@B + kap*(D.T@D) without pinning translational or disconnected-component zero modes before calling cg(H, rhs, x0=u) in line 92.
findings.implication: Because hexagon triangle flips (arms 1 and 2) preserve node degrees and directional edge counts (lines 46-47) but alter the number of collinear two-edge continuations (nb, exported as bends in line 100), mechanical contrasts between arm 1 and arm 2 can be driven by changes in active collinear bending motifs rather than triangle closure itself. Additionally, warm-starting CG on a singular Hessian leaves unconstrained nullspace drift in u.
findings.recommended_check: Compare active bend counts (nb) between arm 1 and arm 2 across all seeds to quantify collinear-motif confounding, and orthogonalize u against global translations (or pin one node per connected component) during CG solves.

findings.title: Restricted dt refinement coverage and undocumented rate cap in first-order operator splitting
findings.evidence: Time integration in source/cpu-sweep.py line 98 uses a first-order explicit operator-splitting update with dt=0.1 and an undocumented rate cap np.minimum(30, 10*np.abs(e-q)), while half-step refinement (ACTUAL_DESIGN.md line 9; analysis/SUMMARY.json lines 13-14) was only performed on 16 cases at L=12, seed 73000, and z_target in {3.2, 4.8}.
findings.implication: The small refinement error (1.83e-4 in analysis/SUMMARY.json line 13) is only demonstrated for well-connected L=12 networks at z >= 3.2 and does not bound time-stepping errors at larger sizes (L=18, 24) or lower coordination (z <= 2.4) where localized non-affine deformations could stiffen exp(10*abs(e-q)).
findings.recommended_check: Extend dt=0.05 refinement checks to L=24 and to all eligible low-z states (z_target=2.0 and 2.4), and log the maximum realized value of 10*abs(e-q) across all trajectories to confirm whether the cap of 30 is ever active.

review.strongest_surviving_claim: Within this small-strain linearized triangular-network model, the quadratic energy assembly, analytic stress computation, and CG equilibrium solver are numerically consistent (directional gradient error 4.02e-16, translational null residual 1.39e-16, maximum production force residual 3.31e-10, and exact 1.0 stress retention across all elastic r=1 controls), and at high coordination (L=24, z_target=4.8, four seeds) fixed-node hub-biased edge replacement co-changes clustering and reduces stress retention by 1.94% (kappa=0.003) to 3.92% (kappa=0.03) relative to uniform networks, whereas degree-preserving triangle-biased versus triangle-suppressed hexagon flips produce near-zero retention differences whose 95% pointwise bootstrap intervals span zero.
review.decisive_next_experiment: Execute the kappa=0, r=0.5 central-force relaxation sweep across all 336 graph variants alongside a matched linear-rate (lambda=1, rate=1 instead of exp(10*abs(e-q))) control at kappa in {0.0, 0.003, 0.03}, and compute pairwise-eligible contrasts separately for arms 1 vs 2 (without conditioning on arm 3 rigidity) while logging collinear bend counts (nb).
